3.186 All breaks in support and discussions concerning them must be recorded in the Support Plan.

Chapter 3h: In-Work Support (IWS) on Confident Futures

3.187 IWS will be provided to Participants who move into employment. For those Participants entering work, and with their consent, you should, complete an Employment Support Plan (ESP) and issue it to the employer within 10 working days of the Participant entering Employment or self-employment.

3.188 IWS will be in place for either the remainder of the Participants time on the programme (up to 365 days from their start date) or until the they no longer require it.

3.189 In the rare event where a Participant does not agree to an ESP being produced, you must ensure this decision is clearly documented, dated, and formally recorded in their Support Plan. Supporting evidence should also be retained to support compliance and assurance activities. If the Participant wants to remain on the programme you should continue to provide tailored IWS to them and continue to update their Support Plan.

3.190 If a Participant moves into employment, remind the Participant to notify their PTWA as per Chapter 3e: Change of Circumstances while on Confident Futures. They may decide they do not require IWS, and they can choose to end their participation in the programme at this point. Refer to Chapter 4: Leaving Confident Futures and Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referral and Payment (PRaP) System for Confident Futures for action to take for completers in this scenario.

Note: You should not request the Participant to notify the PTWA if they are not in receipt of Universal Credit.

3.191 You will be responsible for the design of the ESP which must set out the support you will give to the Participant and the employer during the IWS period, for the duration of the programme (up to 365 calendar days), to help the Participant sustain employment. It will also include the Participant’s support needs from the employer after you are no longer involved, after the period of IWS. The ESP should contain as a minimum:

a description of the IWS you are providing to the Participant

any actions required of the Participant in relation to the IWS

all Non-Confident Futures Activities

3.192 You must provide tailored IWS to both the Participant and the employer to help the Participant stay in work, except where the Participant has stated they do not require it. The IWS should be provided by the same Dedicated Adviser, and to the same frequency and intensity as during the pre-employment support phase.

3.193 The same level of support will be expected for those Participants who choose to become self-employed. It is not intended that you would act in a small business advisor capacity, rather you should continue to support the Participant with on-going management of their barriers to work as you would with an employed Participant. You should signpost the Participant towards agencies that can support them with appropriate business advice, including helping the Participant to access the Access to Work (AtW) provision.

3.194 Support for each Participant must include, but is not limited to:

maintaining frequency of contact (at least once every 4 calendar weeks) with Participant, with any additional contact as required

where appropriate, the Participant being accompanied to the workplace by the Dedicated Adviser, and the Dedicated Adviser supporting the Participant in meetings with the Participant’s line manager and colleagues

on-going engagement with the Participant’s wider sustainable support network (both formal and informal networks)

practical actions, for example socialising and integration in the work environment, journey planning, pre-start visits for familiarisation, establishing a buddy in the workplace

facilitating any reasonable adjustments required and where appropriate, ensuring Access to Work (AtW) assistance is in place from the from the start of employment

3.195 The ESP must be updated when the Participant enters employment or self-employment and at least every 4 calendar weeks throughout IWS. Where Participant has stated they do not want an ESP, you should update the Support Plan.

3.196 Check the possible impact on the Participant’s welfare benefits of any paid employment undertaken and ensure these are understood by the Participant.

Confident Futures employer support offer

3.197 You will be expected to have and to build strong links to national and local employers, helping to build disability confidence and to increase the capacity and sustainability of employers including Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) to recruit and retain disabled people.

3.198 You must provide a full employer support offer focussed on working with the employer so that the employer can continue to support the Participant in work after the provision has ended. The employer support offer will include meeting with employers and their staff and encouraging employers to find champions/advocates within their workplace. This will also involve up-skilling employers and developing a support network that will continue to work together to meet the Participant’s needs and help them to sustain employment.

3.199 You have a role in developing the confidence of the employers you work with in the delivery of the Provision to accommodate disabled people in their workplace and to understand the principles of “Disability Confident”. This includes increasing an employer’s disability awareness and capability. You will need to ensure that employers are able to continue to support each Participant with their support network and AtW where appropriate once the delivery of IWS on Confident Futures ends.

Local tailoring and stakeholder engagement

schools or establishments exempted from registration under the Children Act 1989 or operated on Crown property

3.128 Where your Participant makes alternative arrangements due to barriers to participation, costs should only be reimbursed where the provision of childcare falls into one of the above categories.

3.129 Prior to the reimbursement of childcare costs, you must check that the child or children satisfy the age requirement, are a dependant of and reside with your Participant. Support for childcare costs can be paid for each child up to and including the 31 August, following that child’s sixteenth birthday.

3.130 If your Participant commences work, then you are not responsible for childcare costs connected with that employment. Should you wish to offer to fund childcare costs, this will be at your discretion and needs to comply with any HMRC guidelines and are not claimable from DWP.

3.131 To ensure that you or DWP do not take on liability for the safety of children, you must not recommend any particular childcare facilities to your Participants. It is always the Participant’s responsibility to decide whom they entrust with the care of their children. In addition, whilst you may have crèche facilities or childcare facilities on your premises that adhere to current legislation, it must be the parent’s choice to use those facilities.

Replacement care

3.132 You are expected to provide funding for replacement care costs (other than other childcare cost), to support your Participant in an activity that you have, or are approving, where it has been identified as a barrier for your Participant to achieve agreed goals and objectives for Participants who:

are aged 18 or over

are eligible and currently on the Confident Futures scheme

have spent a significant proportion of their lives providing unpaid support to relatives, partners or friends who are ill, frail, disabled or have a mental health or a substance misuse problem

3.133 Prior to agreeing the payment for replacement care costs, you may wish to consider other alternatives, such as moving the time or date of the activity or meeting. Where this is not possible, and replacement care costs have been accepted, then carers must be participating in an approved activity or attending an interview, which has been arranged by you or an employer.

3.134 You need to ensure prior to agreement of funding for any costs that the replacement care is provided by a Local Authority Registered Provider, a Local Authority Preferred Provider, or a recognised care organisation within the local area.

3.135 To ensure that you or DWP do not take on liability for the safety of the individual requiring care you must not recommend any providers, organisations or facilities to your Participant. It is always the responsibility of the carer or person being cared for to make any arrangements.

Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) checks

3.136 Where your Participant undertakes any activity, in agreement with you, that requires a basic check permitted by the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS), you are responsible for funding any associated costs regarding undertaking this check.

3.137 Note DBS helps employers make safer recruitment decisions each year by processing and issuing DBS checks for England, Wales, the Channel Islands and the Isle of Man. DBS also maintains the adults’ and children’s Barred Lists and makes considered decisions as to whether an individual should be included on one or both of these lists and barred from engaging in regulated activity. Employers will retain the responsibility for the higher-level DBS check if employing your Participant.

Chapter 3e: Change of Circumstances while on Confident Futures

3.138 You must ensure that you hold your Participant’s up to date personal information. Your Participant is responsible for notifying Universal Credit via their Universal Credit account, or by contacting their Jobcentre Plus in writing of any change in their circumstances that occur whilst attending Confident Futures. If you become aware of any change of circumstances which would impact on any benefits your Participant may be in receipt of, you must remind them of their obligation to notify Universal Credit of the change(s).

3.139 The PTWA will send a UCCF01 Change of Circumstances form through unencrypted email to your dedicated inbox with details of any relevant changes to your Participants’ circumstances. In the event of a significant IT failure then a clerical change of circumstances notification form will be issued by the PTWA. If the UCCF01 form is requesting to exit from Confident Futures, it must clearly state one of the exit reasons.

3.140 The PTWA will notify you of the following change of circumstances using the UCCF01 form. This list is not exhaustive:

name

address

phone number

email address

entitlement to benefit and / or change of Labour Market Regime

work search and work availability requirements (including Easements, switching off and tailored conditionality)

appointee / Power of Attorney

outcome of a Self-Employment Gateway Interview

change of Jobcentre and / or PTWA

Participant is in prison or leaves prison

Participant death

exiting the programme

3.141 On receipt of a UCCF01 form you must update your records immediately with any changes to your Participant’s personal information.

3.142 Where the PTWA has notified you on a UCCF01 Change of Circumstances form that a Participants claim to Universal Credit has ended you should discuss whether they wish to continue to participate in Confident Futures.

3.211 Engagement with employers should be ongoing, responsive, and aligned to local labour market conditions. Providers should maintain regular interaction with employers to understand workforce needs, identify suitable vacancies, and develop clear pathways into employment for Participants.

3.212 This approach should be integrated with wider stakeholder engagement activity and designed to ensure that initial engagement progresses into sustained partnerships. These partnerships should support not only recruitment, but also retention and progression for Participants with health conditions or disabilities and align with the wider employer engagement approach set out in the section covering working with employers from paragraph 3.197.

Engagement with DWP and Jobcentre Plus

3.213 It is essential that you build and maintain strong working links with DWP and Jobcentre Plus, maintaining these throughout the duration of your Confident Futures contract. You will have regular contact with Jobcentre Plus Partnership Managers; DWP Performance Managers; and DWP Commercial managers, amongst others in addition to the PTWAs, who you will have frequent engagement with, for example to undertake Warm Handover calls and complete referrals to you. This approach will support collaboration and partnership working along with the sharing of opportunities that can support your Participant’s journey towards achievement of employment.

Chapter 3i: Disruption to business delivery

3.214 In exceptional circumstances it may be necessary for you to implement Business Continuity arrangements during:

government restrictions

localised emergencies which prevent the delivery of full service, for example your delivery building is closed

This list is not exhaustive.

3.215 Where there is a significant risk that changes to working practices and daily routines will be required, and official advice has been issued for example, National Government restriction, you can apply Business Continuity arrangements. You should complete all relevant risk assessments to make decisions on whether closure is most appropriate for the given situation.

3.216 Any face to face appointments that have been scheduled, in agreement with Participants, during the period covered by official advice, may instead be carried out digitally with system notes recorded for audit purposes. In this scenario, providers should expect to receive official confirmation from DWP.

3.217 In some other circumstances that are localised, it may be necessary for providers to consider implementing Business Continuity arrangements locally, this could be where:

extreme weather conditions – red, yellow or amber weather warnings have been issued

strike action affecting local transportation network

local emergency or incident, for example building closures

This list is not exhaustive.

3.218 Where locally there is an increased risk that changes to working practices and daily routines will be required, appropriate risk assessments should be carried out. If it is then considered safe to do so, business as usual working arrangements should apply.

3.219 Where you are unable to deliver full service due to the scenarios, described in the paragraphs above, decisions should be made in consultation with your Performance Manager.

3.220 For all National and Local restrictions or Emergencies listed above, Business Continuity arrangements should be ready to be implemented. Where a scheduled face to face appointment cannot take place, and is carried out digitally instead, detailed system notes should be recorded for audit purposes. This information must be retained for audit purposes in the Support Plan.

Chapter 4: Leaving Confident Futures

4.1 This chapter sets out the steps that you and PTWA will take to ensure that all Confident Futures Participants complete at the appropriate stage in their journey. The Customer Service Standard covered in this chapter is Customer Service Standard 3.

4.2 A Participant will become an Early Completer when they finish on provision before the Six-Month Touchpoint (between the day they start on the programme (day 1) and up to and including day 182 of their participation).

4.3 A Participant will become a Completer when they finish on provision between day 183 and day 365.
